2608.15147.title: Constitutive Priors for Machine Intelligence: A Legitimacy Theory of the Artificial Physical World
2608.15147.paper_summary: Machine intelligence has conquered the symbolic world but stalled at the physical one. The stall is structural: physical AI faces a cold-start deadlock -- no intelligence without data, no data without deployed intelligence. Our thesis: the deadlock is real but unevenly distributed, and the exception has a name: the artificial physical world. Buildings, industrial facilities, and infrastructure are intentionally constituted and documented: designed artifacts ship with readable archives that precede and constitute their instances; here, norms are promulgated before instances, not averaged from them. Four contributions. (i) From a four-world ontology we derive a legitimacy criterion for constitutive prior frameworks: prior extraction is legitimate if and only if the object domain is intentionally constituted and has left a readable archive; the criterion is testable through direction of fit -- deviation from a constitutive norm is a violation in the world, not a revision of the model. (ii) We establish a layering lower bound: any such framework has at least four layers -- syntax, concept, knowledge, instance -- because four construction goals pair into mutually incompatible carriers. (iii) We register deployment claims across five industrial domains and a 32-class failure-mode vocabulary. (iv) We stake the framework on five falsifiable predictions, the central one checkable on the public engineering record: if it fails, the framework fails. Semi-formal arguments back these claims (Appendix A): a Gold-type boundary on rule coverage in archiveless worlds, a decidability result for failure reduction over closed concept layers, and a boundary theorem for certificate-anchored calculi. Large language models find an honored place here -- as readers of the archive, not as the archive. First of three companion works; the companions take up the questions deliberately left open.
2608.15147.paper_summary_zh: 機器智慧已征服了符號世界，但在物理世界卻停滯不前。這種停滯是結構性的：物理人工智慧面臨著冷啟動的僵局——沒有數據就沒有智慧，沒有部署的智慧就沒有數據。我們的論點是：這個僵局是真實存在的，但分佈不均，而例外有一個名字：人工物理世界。建築、工業設施和基礎設施是有意構成和記錄的：設計的工藝品附帶可讀的檔案，這些檔案在其實例之前並構成了它們；在這裡，規範是在實例之前頒布的，而不是從實例中平均得出的。四項貢獻。(i) 從四世界本體論中，我們推導出一個構成性先前框架的合法性標準：只有當對象領域是有意構成並且留下可讀的檔案時，先前的提取才是合法的；該標準可以通過適合方向進行測試——偏離構成性規範是對世界的違反，而不是對模型的修訂。(ii) 我們建立了一個分層下限：任何這樣的框架至少有四個層次——語法、概念、知識、實例——因為四個建設目標配對成為互相不相容的承載體。(iii) 我們在五個工業領域和一個32類故障模式詞彙中登記了部署聲明。(iv) 我們在五個可證偽的預測上建立了框架，其中中央預測可以在公共工程記錄中檢查：如果它失敗，框架就失敗。半正式的論證支持這些聲明（附錄A）：在沒有檔案的世界中對規則覆蓋的金邊界，對於封閉概念層的故障減少的可判定性結果，以及對於證書錨定計算的邊界定理。大型語言模型在這裡找到了榮譽的位置——作為檔案的讀者，而不是檔案。這是三部伴隨作品中的第一部；伴隨作品將探討故意留出的問題。
